claims.claim_text: The indexed Alfred P. Daignault is confirmed as the enlisted soldier in the official Army record and the corporal listed by the OSS Assessment Staff.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Alfred P. Daignault, B.S., Cpl. W, C, I, K, H
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index and Army row share an exact private identifier and full name; the direct OSS staff list independently supplies the same full name and enlisted grade.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by a unique private identifier and exact full name, with independent direct OSS staff-list corroboration; the identifier is withheld from public data.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry to 14 August 1942. The OSS source records later corporal rank and assessment stations but does not establish the transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The OSS staff instructions print predecessor institutions in parentheses; none follows Daignault's entry, so no institution or employer is inferred from that silence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed 2nd Lt. George E. Dail Jr. is a high-confidence match to Lieutenant George Dail of the OSS Morale Operations unit in China.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In May, Lieutenant George Dail joined the MO unit and took over its administrative duties
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A scholarly history based on OSS records places a Lieutenant George Dail in the China Morale Operations unit and describes his administrative assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon full surname-name combination, matching lieutenant grade and direct OSS China context. The book omits the middle initial and suffix.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source describes a wartime May assignment within OSS. It does not document pre-OSS employment or the date George Dail first entered OSS service.
claims.match_notes: A different 2nd Lt. George W. Dail of the 117th Infantry was killed in Europe and is rejected as a namesake; his middle initial and service context conflict.
